title: CHEMISTRY Paper 01 - General Proficiency
instructions: This test consists of 60 items. You will have 1 hour and 15 minutes to answer them.
In addition to this test booklet, you should have an answer sheet.
Each item in this test has four suggested answers lettered (A), (B), (C), (D). Read each item you are about to answer and decide which choice is best.

On your answer sheet, find the number which corresponds to your item and shade the space having the same letter as the answer you have chosen. Look at the sample item below. Sample Item: The SI unit of length is the (A) metre (B) newton (C) second (D) kilogram. The best answer to this item is "metre", so (A) has been shaded.
If you want to change your answer, erase it completely before you fill in your new choice.
When you are told to begin, turn the page and work as quickly and as carefully as you can. If you cannot answer an item, go on to the next one. You may return to that item later.
You may do any rough work in this booklet.
Figures are not necessarily drawn to scale.
You may use a silent, non-programmable calculator to answer items.

2020-JAN-D01.alt: Equation: displayed formula of ethene (H₂C=CH₂) + Cl₂ gives the displayed formula of 1,2-dichloroethane, with one Cl on each carbon.

2020-JAN-D02.alt: Graph of pH (vertical axis, marked 1, 7 and 13) against Volume of Solution Y added (cm³). The pH starts at about 1, rises slowly, then rises steeply through 7 and levels off at about 13.

2020-JAN-D03A.alt: Option A: two overlapping circles. The overlap holds one cross and one dot; the left circle has no other electrons and the right circle has six other crosses.

2020-JAN-D03B.alt: Option B: two overlapping circles. The overlap holds two crosses and two dots (two shared pairs); the left circle has four other crosses and the right circle four other dots.

2020-JAN-D03C.alt: Option C: two overlapping circles. The overlap holds three crosses and three dots (three shared pairs); each circle has two other electrons.

2020-JAN-D03D.alt: Option D: two overlapping circles. The overlap holds one cross and one dot; the left circle has six other dots and the right circle six other crosses.

2020-JAN-D04.alt: Graph of Temperature (°C) against Volume of acid added (cm³). The temperature rises in a straight line through point P to a peak at point Q, then falls in a straight line through points R and S.

2020-JAN-D05A.alt: Option A: graph of Total volume of CO₂ (cm³) against Time (min). The curve rises steeply from the origin, then levels off.

2020-JAN-D05B.alt: Option B: graph of Total volume of CO₂ (cm³) against Time (min). The curve starts high and falls, levelling off near the time axis.

2020-JAN-D05C.alt: Option C: graph of Total volume of CO₂ (cm³) against Time (min). A straight line falls from high on the volume axis to the time axis.

2020-JAN-D05D.alt: Option D: graph of Total volume of CO₂ (cm³) against Time (min). A straight line rises steadily from the origin.

2020-JAN-D06.alt: Conductivity apparatus: a 6 V DC supply and a bulb in a circuit connected to two graphite rods that dip into a container of the substance under investigation.

2020-JAN-D08.alt: Reaction sequence: FeCO₃ goes to FeO (stage I), FeO goes to Fe₂O₃ (stage II), Fe₂O₃ goes to Fe₂(SO₄)₃ (stage III), and Fe₂(SO₄)₃ goes to Fe(OH)₃ (stage IV).

2020-JAN-D09.alt: Two displayed formulae. Compound I: a three-carbon chain with OH on the middle carbon (propan-2-ol). Compound II: a three-carbon chain with OH on the end carbon (propan-1-ol).

2020-JAN-D10.alt: Small displayed formula of ethene, H₂C=CH₂, shown as option A's 'structural formula'.

2020-JAN-D11.alt: Three displayed formulae. Q: CH₃-CH₂-COOH (propanoic acid). R: CH₃-COO-CH₃ (methyl ethanoate). S: CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-O-H (propan-1-ol).

2020-JAN-D12A.alt: Option A: displayed formula of butane with Br on the first carbon (1-bromobutane).

2020-JAN-D12B.alt: Option B: displayed formula CH₂=C(Br)-CH₂-CH₃, with a C=C double bond and Br on the second carbon.

2020-JAN-D12C.alt: Option C: displayed formula of butane with Br on the second carbon (2-bromobutane).

2020-JAN-D12D.alt: Option D: displayed formula of a three-carbon chain with a CH₃ branch and Br both on the middle carbon (2-bromo-2-methylpropane).

2020-JAN-D13A.alt: Option A: displayed formula of ethane, CH₃-CH₃.

2020-JAN-D13B.alt: Option B: displayed formula of ethene, H₂C=CH₂.

2020-JAN-D13C.alt: Option C: displayed formula of propane, CH₃-CH₂-CH₃.

2020-JAN-D13D.alt: Option D: displayed formula of propane drawn with a bend (single bonds only).

2020-JAN-D14.alt: Monomer: displayed formula H-C(H)(NH₂)-COOH, a carbon atom bonded to two H atoms, an NH₂ group and a COOH group (glycine, an amino acid).
